scope: CPU double-precision numerical integration comparison only; not a rendered image or visual acceptance.

source.equations: sliceAt, columnLight, incidentAt; WGSL lines 51-101, including h/reach, area-cell weight, soft coupling kernel, and the 10x4 midpoint loops.
source.geometry: The exact R3 preview origin/end/width values were used to define normal and giant travel, half-span and front; source phase, width and drive equations are transcribed from fragment lines 123-129.

method.relativeErrorRule: Reported only where dense-reference luminance Y > 0.005; lower-emission points were excluded from relative ranking.

findings.interpretation: The 160x64 reference is numerically converged relative to 80x32 at the reported maximum-error point, while the 10x4 shader quadrature differs by about 9.4% Y there. Across sampled meaningful points, the largest relative Y discrepancy is about 12.9%. This is a specific source-area quadrature-resolution discrepancy and can justify an isolated R5 numerical-resolution experiment with the source shape, incident radiance, material law, timing, and host held fixed. It does not establish visible banding, a visual defect, or a quality improvement.

limits: CPU integration of the exact source equations; no full WGSL execution, GPU output, raster pixels, actual screen size, ordinary-speed viewing, or audio acceptance.
Finite point selection and preview geometry; this does not characterize every receiver coordinate or all screen sizes.
No R5 code or integration-resolution alternative was implemented or evaluated here.
